papers.title: PCIPG2.0: Multi-omics fusion and structure-aware graph autoencoding for protein complex identification
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Protein complexes execute cellular functions, yet identifying them from protein–protein interaction (PPI) networks remains challenging because interactomes are incomplete and purely topology-driven clustering often lacks mechanistic interpretability. Here we present PCIPG 2.0, an unsupervised framework that explicitly addresses two major bottlenecks in PPI-based complex discovery: missing interactions and limited mechanistic specificity. PCIPG 2.0 first fuses multiple omics views to prioritize high-confidence candidate protein associations and enhance the observed interactome, and then learns structure-aware node representations by aggregating residue embeddings on residue graphs, coupled with a PPI-level graph autoencoder to infer latent complex memberships. Results Across five yeast benchmarks, PCIPG 2.0 consistently improves complex recovery over representative baselines and yields predicted complexes with significantly higher Gene Ontology semantic coherence than size-matched random sets. Literature-supported case studies and AlphaFold3-based assembly analyses further suggest that representative predictions are consistent with functionally coherent and structurally plausible protein assemblies. Together, these results suggest that combining multi-omics-driven interactome completion with residue-informed representation learning provides a useful and mechanistically informed framework for protein complex identification under incomplete interactome measurements. Availability The source code is available at GitHub https://github.com/hyx-1/PCIPG2.0 . The complete reproducibility package, including the code, processed data, configuration files and materials required to reproduce the experiments reported in this manuscript, has been archived on Zenodo with an archival DOI https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20133228 . The GitHub repository also provides the README-based usage instructions

papers.title: Empowering Chemical Structures with Biological Insights for Scalable Phenotypic Virtual Screening
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation The scalable identification of bioactive compounds is essential for contemporary drug discovery. This process faces a key trade-off: structural screening offers scalability but lacks biological context, whereas high-content phenotypic profiling provides deep biological insights but is resource-intensive. The primary challenge is to extract robust biological signals from noisy data and encode them into representations that do not require biological data at inference. Results This study presents DECODE (DEcomposing Cellular Observations of Drug Effects), a framework that bridges this gap by empowering chemical representations with intrinsic biological semantics to enable structure-based in silico biological profiling. DECODE leverages limited paired transcriptomic and morphological data as supervisory signals during training, enabling the extraction of a measurement-invariant biological fingerprint from chemical structures and explicit filtering of modality-specific variation. Across held-out retrieval, scaffold-split and UMAP-clustering virtual-screening benchmarks, DECODE improves functional retrieval and early active-compound prioritization over baselines. Availability and implementation The codes and datasets of DECODE are available at https://github.com/lian-xiao/DECODE

llm_highlights_zh: 这个过程面临着一个关键的权衡：结构筛选提供了可扩展性，但缺乏生物学背景，而高内涵表型分析提供了深入的生物学见解，但资源密集型。
主要挑战是从噪声数据中提取鲁棒的生物信号，并将其编码为推理时不需要生物数据的表示形式。
本研究提出了 DECODE（分解药物作用的细胞观察），这是一个框架，通过赋予化学表示与内在的生物语义以实现基于结构的计算机生物分析，从而弥补了这一差距。

papers.title: BCAR: A fast and indel-tolerant barcode-sequence mapper
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation DNA barcodes are commonly used as a tool to distinguish genuine mutations from sequencing errors in sequencing-based assays. In the presence of indel errors, utilizing barcodes requires accurate alignment of the raw reads to distinguish genuine indels from indel errors. Existing strategies to do this generally rely on aligners built for homology comparison and do not fully utilize quality scores. We reasoned that developing an aligner purpose-built for error correction could yield higher quality barcode-sequence maps. Results Here, we present BCAR, a fast barcode-sequence mapper for correcting sequencing errors. BCAR considers all of the evidence for each base call at each position both during alignment and during final consensus generation. BCAR creates high-accuracy barcode-sequence maps from simulated reads across a broad range of error rates and read lengths, outperforming existing methods. We apply BCAR to two experimental datasets, where it generates high-quality barcode-sequence maps. Availability and implementation BCAR source code, documentation, and test data are available from: https://github.com/dry-brews/BCAR or https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20088816

papers.primary_summary_zh: DNA 条形码通常用作在基于测序的检测中区分真正突变和测序错误的工具。在存在插入缺失错误的情况下，利用条形码需要准确比对原始读数，以区分真正的插入缺失和插入缺失错误。现有的策略通常依赖于为同源性比较而构建的对齐器，并且没有充分利用质量分数。我们推断，开发专门用于纠错的对准器可以产生更高质量的条形码序列图。结果在这里，我们展示了 BCAR，一种用于纠正测序错误的快速条形码序列映射器。 BCAR 在比对期间和最终共识生成期间考虑每个位置的每个碱基检出的所有证据。 BCAR 通过各种错误率和读取长度的模拟读取创建高精度条形码序列图，其性能优于现有方法。我们将 BCAR 应用于两个实验数据集，生成高质量的条形码序列图。可用性和实施​​ BCAR 源代码、文档和测试数据可从以下位置获取：https://github.com/dry-brews/BCAR 或 https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20088816

papers.title: AstroLogics: A simulation-based framework for the analysis of Boolean model ensembles
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Boolean networks (BNs) have emerged as versatile tools for modeling cellular regulatory mechanisms due to their ability to capture key biological features despite their simplicity. Multiple BN synthesis methods have emerged in recent decades, aiming to infer BNs with dynamics that correspond to experimental data. Often, these methods generate multiple BN candidates or "model ensembles". While these ensembles are valuable for representing cell populations and their heterogeneity, they are typically treated as single components without examining their constituent features. Results We present AstroLogics, a novel framework designed to analyze and identify differences in both dynamical behavior and logical regulation within a BN model ensemble. The framework calculates dynamical distances between BNs through exploration of their state transition graphs (STGs), enabling clustering of similarly functioning models that may represent different cellular fates or signaling mechanisms. AstroLogics also identifies key logical properties that govern each cluster, highlighting the core regulatory structures that differentiate model behaviors. Our approach leverages MaBoSS, a stochastic simulation tool that implements the Boolean Kinetic Monte-Carlo algorithm to address time interpretation in BNs. This probabilistic estimation method allows efficient probing of BN dynamics through stochastic simulations, overcoming the computational limitations of exhaustive STG analysis. Our framework also provides powerful visualization and classification of the BN ensemble. Through multiple use cases, we demonstrate how AstroLogics facilitates comprehensive analyses of model diversity and discovery of key regulatory structures within a BN ensemble. Availability and Implementation The AstroLogics package, along with tutorials and datasets, is available at https://github.com/sysbio-curie/AstroLogics

all_papers.title: PCIPG2.0: Multi-omics fusion and structure-aware graph autoencoding for protein complex identification
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Protein complexes execute cellular functions, yet identifying them from protein–protein interaction (PPI) networks remains challenging because interactomes are incomplete and purely topology-driven clustering often lacks mechanistic interpretability. Here we present PCIPG 2.0, an unsupervised framework that explicitly addresses two major bottlenecks in PPI-based complex discovery: missing interactions and limited mechanistic specificity. PCIPG 2.0 first fuses multiple omics views to prioritize high-confidence candidate protein associations and enhance the observed interactome, and then learns structure-aware node representations by aggregating residue embeddings on residue graphs, coupled with a PPI-level graph autoencoder to infer latent complex memberships. Results Across five yeast benchmarks, PCIPG 2.0 consistently improves complex recovery over representative baselines and yields predicted complexes with significantly higher Gene Ontology semantic coherence than size-matched random sets. Literature-supported case studies and AlphaFold3-based assembly analyses further suggest that representative predictions are consistent with functionally coherent and structurally plausible protein assemblies. Together, these results suggest that combining multi-omics-driven interactome completion with residue-informed representation learning provides a useful and mechanistically informed framework for protein complex identification under incomplete interactome measurements. Availability The source code is available at GitHub https://github.com/hyx-1/PCIPG2.0 . The complete reproducibility package, including the code, processed data, configuration files and materials required to reproduce the experiments reported in this manuscript, has been archived on Zenodo with an archival DOI https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20133228 . The GitHub repository also provides the README-based usage instructions

llm_highlights_zh: 在这里，我们提出 PCIPG 2.0，这是一个无监督框架，它明确解决了基于 PPI 的复杂发现中的两个主要瓶颈：交互缺失和机械特异性有限。
PCIPG 2.0 首先融合多个组学视图，优先考虑高可信度候选蛋白质关联并增强观察到的相互作用组，然后通过聚合残基图上的残基嵌入来学习结构感知节点表示，并结合 PPI 级图自动编码器来推断潜在的复杂成员资格。
在五个酵母基准中，PCIPG 2.0 持续提高了代表性基线的复合物回收率，并产生了比大小匹配的随机集具有显着更高的基因本体语义一致性的预测复合物。

all_papers.title: Empowering Chemical Structures with Biological Insights for Scalable Phenotypic Virtual Screening
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation The scalable identification of bioactive compounds is essential for contemporary drug discovery. This process faces a key trade-off: structural screening offers scalability but lacks biological context, whereas high-content phenotypic profiling provides deep biological insights but is resource-intensive. The primary challenge is to extract robust biological signals from noisy data and encode them into representations that do not require biological data at inference. Results This study presents DECODE (DEcomposing Cellular Observations of Drug Effects), a framework that bridges this gap by empowering chemical representations with intrinsic biological semantics to enable structure-based in silico biological profiling. DECODE leverages limited paired transcriptomic and morphological data as supervisory signals during training, enabling the extraction of a measurement-invariant biological fingerprint from chemical structures and explicit filtering of modality-specific variation. Across held-out retrieval, scaffold-split and UMAP-clustering virtual-screening benchmarks, DECODE improves functional retrieval and early active-compound prioritization over baselines. Availability and implementation The codes and datasets of DECODE are available at https://github.com/lian-xiao/DECODE

all_papers.llm_title_bilingual: 利用生物学见解增强化学结构，实现可扩展的表型虚拟筛选 / Empowering Chemical Structures with Biological Insights for Scalable Phenotypic Virtual Screening
all_papers.llm_research_question_zh: 生物活性化合物的可扩展鉴定对于当代药物发现至关重要。
llm_highlights_zh: 这个过程面临着一个关键的权衡：结构筛选提供了可扩展性，但缺乏生物学背景，而高内涵表型分析提供了深入的生物学见解，但资源密集型。
主要挑战是从噪声数据中提取鲁棒的生物信号，并将其编码为推理时不需要生物数据的表示形式。
本研究提出了 DECODE（分解药物作用的细胞观察），这是一个框架，通过赋予化学表示与内在的生物语义以实现基于结构的计算机生物分析，从而弥补了这一差距。

all_papers.primary_summary_raw: The scalable identification of bioactive compounds is essential for contemporary drug discovery. This process faces a key trade-off: structural screening offers scalability but lacks biological context, whereas high-content phenotypic profiling provides deep biological insights but is resource-intensive. The primary challenge is to extract robust biological signals from noisy data and encode them into representations that do not require biological data at inference. Results This study presents DECODE (DEcomposing Cellular Observations of Drug Effects), a framework that bridges this gap by empowering chemical representations with intrinsic biological semantics to enable structure-based in silico biological profiling. DECODE leverages limited paired transcriptomic and morphological data as supervisory signals during training, enabling the extraction of a measurement-invariant biological fingerprint from chemical structures and explicit filtering of modality-specific variation. Across held-out retrieval, scaffold-split and UMAP-clustering virtual-screening benchmarks, DECODE improves functional retrieval and early active-compound prioritization over baselines.

all_papers.title: BCAR: A fast and indel-tolerant barcode-sequence mapper
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation DNA barcodes are commonly used as a tool to distinguish genuine mutations from sequencing errors in sequencing-based assays. In the presence of indel errors, utilizing barcodes requires accurate alignment of the raw reads to distinguish genuine indels from indel errors. Existing strategies to do this generally rely on aligners built for homology comparison and do not fully utilize quality scores. We reasoned that developing an aligner purpose-built for error correction could yield higher quality barcode-sequence maps. Results Here, we present BCAR, a fast barcode-sequence mapper for correcting sequencing errors. BCAR considers all of the evidence for each base call at each position both during alignment and during final consensus generation. BCAR creates high-accuracy barcode-sequence maps from simulated reads across a broad range of error rates and read lengths, outperforming existing methods. We apply BCAR to two experimental datasets, where it generates high-quality barcode-sequence maps. Availability and implementation BCAR source code, documentation, and test data are available from: https://github.com/dry-brews/BCAR or https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20088816

all_papers.title: AstroLogics: A simulation-based framework for the analysis of Boolean model ensembles
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Boolean networks (BNs) have emerged as versatile tools for modeling cellular regulatory mechanisms due to their ability to capture key biological features despite their simplicity. Multiple BN synthesis methods have emerged in recent decades, aiming to infer BNs with dynamics that correspond to experimental data. Often, these methods generate multiple BN candidates or "model ensembles". While these ensembles are valuable for representing cell populations and their heterogeneity, they are typically treated as single components without examining their constituent features. Results We present AstroLogics, a novel framework designed to analyze and identify differences in both dynamical behavior and logical regulation within a BN model ensemble. The framework calculates dynamical distances between BNs through exploration of their state transition graphs (STGs), enabling clustering of similarly functioning models that may represent different cellular fates or signaling mechanisms. AstroLogics also identifies key logical properties that govern each cluster, highlighting the core regulatory structures that differentiate model behaviors. Our approach leverages MaBoSS, a stochastic simulation tool that implements the Boolean Kinetic Monte-Carlo algorithm to address time interpretation in BNs. This probabilistic estimation method allows efficient probing of BN dynamics through stochastic simulations, overcoming the computational limitations of exhaustive STG analysis. Our framework also provides powerful visualization and classification of the BN ensemble. Through multiple use cases, we demonstrate how AstroLogics facilitates comprehensive analyses of model diversity and discovery of key regulatory structures within a BN ensemble. Availability and Implementation The AstroLogics package, along with tutorials and datasets, is available at https://github.com/sysbio-curie/AstroLogics

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh: 布尔网络 (BN) 已成为建模细胞调节机制的通用工具，因为它们尽管简单，但仍能够捕获关键的生物学特征。近几十年来出现了多种BN合成方法，旨在推断具有与实验数据相对应的动力学的BN。通常，这些方法会生成多个 BN 候选者或“模型集合”。虽然这些集合对于代表细胞群及其异质性很有价值，但它们通常被视为单个组件而不检查其组成特征。结果我们提出了 AstroLogics，这是一种新颖的框架，旨在分析和识别 BN 模型集合中动态行为和逻辑调节的差异。该框架通过探索 BN 的状态转换图 (STG) 来计算 BN 之间的动态距离，从而能够对可能代表不同细胞命运或信号机制的相似功能模型进行聚类。 AstroLogics 还确定了管理每个集群的关键逻辑属性，突出了区分模型行为的核心监管结构。我们的方法利用 MaBoSS，这是一种随机模拟工具，它实现了布尔动力学蒙特卡罗算法来解决 BN 中的时间解释问题。这种概率估计方法允许通过随机模拟有效地探测 BN 动力学，克服了详尽的 STG 分析的计算限制。我们的框架还提供强大的 BN 集成可视化和分类功能。通过多个用例，我们展示了 AstroLogics 如何促进对 BN 集成中模型多样性的全面分析和关键监管结构的发现。 可用性和实施​​ AstroLogics 包以及教程和数据集可从 https://github.com/sysbio-curie/AstroLogics 获取
